effective_date_policy: Rates are the standard list prices published at the source on source_checked, with no scheduled future change applied ahead of its effective date. A run reports rate_table_version so a figure can be tied to the prices it used; it does not reprice historical usage at the rates in force on the day that usage occurred.
note: Rates are decimal strings so that loading them introduces no binary floating-point error. Cache rates are derived from the input rate using the multipliers below rather than stored per model, because the published pricing defines them that way. A model whose published cache pricing departs from the table's multipliers carries its own cache_multipliers block, which overrides only the tiers it names.

Tier prices cross-checked against https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing. Ultrafast is not resolved by the Codex adapter and remains an unknown tier.

gpt-6.1-terra.note: Standard list rates; Fast is 2x. Above 272K prompt tokens, input/cache rates double and output is 1.5x. Cross-checked against https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing. Codex records unsplit cache writes in write_5m without a lifetime claim; this row uses the published 30-minute write rate (1.25x input). The inert write_1h slot repeats that rate, as in existing Codex rows; it does not price 12-hour retention (published at 2.5x input), which the adapter cannot distinguish. Unknown and Ultrafast tiers remain unpriced.

gpt-5.5.note: API-key Codex model; Standard list rates. GPT-5.5 and earlier incur no additional cache-write charge (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching), so separately recorded write tokens cost ordinary input rates, with no lifetime distinction. Above 272K input tokens, Standard input/cache rates double and output is 1.5x. Fast is deliberately omitted: no >272K Fast price is published, and this table cannot express a speed-specific context limit.
